waveMode_desc: Select mode: 2D two-source ripple tank, 1D transverse string wave, or 1D longitudinal sound compression
amplitude1_desc: Maximum oscillation amplitude of the first wave source in cm
amplitude2_desc: Maximum oscillation amplitude of the second wave source in cm
waveSpeed_desc: Propagation speed of wave fronts in the medium in cm/s
sourceSeparation_desc: Distance between the two point sources in the ripple tank in cm
phaseDifference_desc: Initial phase difference between the sources in degrees (0 to 360)
damping_desc: Spatial/temporal attenuation coefficient due to medium friction
real_speed_effect: In real mode, wave speed depends on medium elasticity and density
real_damping_effect: In real mode, viscous damping leads to exponential amplitude decay
formula_waveEquation_desc: Displacement of medium particles at position x and time t is a sinusoidal function
formula_wavelength_desc: Wave propagation speed equals the product of wavelength and frequency
formula_superposition_desc: Total displacement at any point equals the algebraic sum of individual wave displacements
formula_constructive_desc: Path difference is an integer multiple of full wavelength
formula_destructive_desc: Path difference is an odd half-integer multiple of wavelength
theoryP1: When two waves propagate through the same medium and overlap, they pass through each other without altering each other's waveform. Within the overlap region, the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements (Principle of Linear Superposition).
theoryP2: For two coherent point sources, constructive interference occurs at points where the path difference is an integer multiple of the wavelength (Δr = mλ), generating antinodal lines of reinforced amplitude. Destructive interference occurs where the path difference is an odd half-wavelength (Δr = (m + 0.5)λ), forming quiet nodal lines where waves cancel out.
theoryP3: Transverse waves feature particle oscillations perpendicular to the direction of propagation, whereas longitudinal waves oscillate parallel to propagation, generating traveling zones of compression and rarefaction.
